headline: Clouds are visible reminders that nothing in nature stays still
universal_truth: What seems solid is often just gathered particles waiting to disperse
fun_facts: The average cumulus cloud weighs about 1.1 million pounds—yet floats because air below is even denser
A single thunderstorm can contain enough water vapor to fill an Olympic swimming pool every second
There are over 100 different types of clouds classified by meteorologists
discussion_questions: What 'clouds' in your life looked solid but turned out to be temporary?
How does knowing something is impermanent change how you experience it?
What would you do differently if you truly believed everything passes?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Look up. Those clouds drifting by are actually flying rivers—some holding more water than flows through the Amazon. They seem so weightless, yet a single cloud can weigh over a million pounds. How is that possible?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: A million-pound cloud floating in the sky seems impossible. We're told heavy things fall. So what's keeping all that water suspended above us?
cliff.prompt: Why don't clouds fall to the ground?

options.text: The water droplets are incredibly small and light
options.response: Yes! Each droplet is so tiny that air resistance keeps it suspended.

options.text: Warm air pushes them up constantly
options.response: Updrafts do help, but there's a simpler reason...

q1.title: Million-Pound Floaters
q1.script: That fluffy cumulus cloud overhead weighs about 1.1 million pounds. But each water droplet is just 0.02 millimeters across—so small that air molecules bouncing around can keep them suspended. It's like dust floating in a sunbeam.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Million-Pound Floaters"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Sky Rivers
q2.script: Atmospheric rivers—long, narrow bands of water vapor—can carry 15 times more water than the Mississippi River. These invisible rivers in the sky bring most of the West Coast's water supply.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: 100 Cloud Types
q3.script: Meteorologists classify over 100 different cloud types. From wispy cirrus at 40,000 feet to ground-hugging stratus, each tells a story about what's happening in the atmosphere. Clouds are weather's messengers.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Clouds remind us that even massive things are temporary. They gather, they disperse, they reform somewhere new. Our problems, our joys, our worries—they're all clouds passing through the sky of our lives.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 3. Tomorrow, we'll follow light itself and discover how it travels. Until then, look up—those clouds have stories to tell.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Perspective - Cloud Watching
growTrack.activity: Spend 3 minutes today watching clouds. Don't analyze—just observe. Notice how they change shape. This simple practice builds your attention muscle and reminds you that everything is in motion.
